response.markdown_report:
**Evidence and directions.** Three starting-point insights guide the next experiment. First, all four perturbation panels completed zero users because dataset routing was unavailable. Explicit routes and coverage checks are therefore prerequisites for interpreting sensitivity. Second, Electronics has a 13.59% sampled training-pair inversion rate. This motivates investigation but does not identify a recency failure or establish validation accuracy. Third, deletion changes both content and positions. Fixed-slot replacements and multiset-preserving swaps provide complementary controls, although neither establishes realistic counterfactual behavior.

Three literature insights sharpen the design. Activation-patching research shows that corruption choices affect conclusions [1]. Recommendation probes should consequently report intervention-specific effects rather than universal importance. Positional-attention research separates positional relations from item semantics [2]. This motivates testing positional regularization separately from item regularization. Sampled ranking metrics can disagree with catalog rankings [3]. Diagnostic ranks must therefore remain separate from the pinned selection metric and required full-catalog recommendations.

**Framework.** Organize experiments along three axes: intervention locus (item identity, order, positional representation), evidence level (fitted-target sensitivity, controlled training comparison, host validation), and coverage (individual user, dataset, four-dataset macro). The main gap is a completed, explicitly routed comparison linking a narrowly defined regularizer to host outcomes.

**Candidate ideas.** Scores are originality/potential/difficulty; higher difficulty means more implementation work.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Routed fixed-slot recency audit | 3/6/3 | Reproducible foundation with inexpensive controls | Measurement alone offers no training improvement |
| Positional-contribution dropout with matched item control [1,2] | 4/7/4 | Small intervention with interpretable component comparison | Established regularization; benefits may reflect generic noise |
| Candidate-distribution stress audit [3] | 3/6/5 | Tests whether easy negatives conceal ranking weaknesses | Catalog scoring costs compute and fitted targets limit inference |

**Selected idea: controlled positional regularization.** At 10% progress, compare unchanged SASRec with dropout applied only to its positional contribution and an identically parameterized item-contribution control. Freeze probability 0.1 before observing new outcomes; preserve existing embedding dropout in every arm. Mask each contribution using inverted elementwise dropout immediately before addition. This tests an operational regularizer, without asserting that older interactions are harmful.

First repair explicit category routing and complete the fixed-slot diagnostic panel. Use fitted final-training targets, frozen candidate sets, unchanged-input checks, replacements preserving the final conditioning item, and earlier-position swaps. Report coverage and paired rank effects separately by category. Run the same frozen panel on each trained arm; comparisons are descriptive, not prospective evidence that diagnostics select interventions.

Train all arms under identical schedules and select solely by pinned macro validation HR@10. Preserve seeds, splits, environment-controlled epochs, dataset routes, predictor generation, and diagnostic interfaces. Launch comparisons only when their compute ceilings fit the remaining shared budget; report incomplete comparisons explicitly. No measured improvement is currently available.

References: [1] https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.16042; [2] https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.02793; [3] https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/

idea.description: Test positional-contribution dropout against unchanged SASRec and a matched item-contribution dropout control, after repairing explicit diagnostic dataset routing. Use completed, position-preserving fitted-target probes to characterize changes, and independently select using the pinned four-category macro validation HR@10.
idea.motivation: The available perturbation results contain no completed users, so they cannot support a diagnostic deployment rule. Electronics shows weaker sampled training separation, but neither those margins nor qualitative feedback identifies positional overreliance. A small controlled regularization experiment is feasible at early research progress and directly tests whether positional regularization provides value beyond another source of embedding noise.
idea.implementation_notes:
Keep DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, original splits, and artifacts beneath the trial directory. Honor SASREC_EPOCHS, defaulting to 200 in the matched environment. Do not inspect hidden test files or fetch external data or pretrained weights.

Implement three declared arms: baseline, positional dropout, and item dropout. Fix additional dropout probability at 0.1. In the existing SASRec embedding computation, identify the item and positional contributions immediately before their addition. Apply inverted elementwise dropout only to the assigned contribution during training; retain existing embedding dropout identically in all arms. Preserve padding masks and zero padded inputs after composition as required by baseline behavior. At evaluation, the additional dropout is identity. Record the exact insertion point and configuration in each checkpoint. Update the predictor writer to reconstruct the trained module and load its checkpoint; evaluation logits should match those of the training module in eval mode on identical inputs.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Explicitly attach dataset_name to each view or provide diagnostic_views keyed by the four required dataset names. Never infer a dataset from local item IDs. Permit category-local probe calls; aggregate only when all four corresponding results are available. Missing routing must produce an actionable unavailable status rather than silently evaluating the wrong catalog.

Reuse the starting idea's bounded panel: up to 32 eligible training users/category, final training item as fitted diagnostic target, target plus 99 unique training-history-excluded negatives, five matched fixed-slot replacements for recent and older positions, and a recent/older swap preserving the final conditioning item. Freeze user IDs, sequence slots, candidates, replacements, and matching statistics from the verified baseline for all arms. Report eligibility, completed users, matching residuals, unchanged-score discrepancies, target-rank changes, and paired recent-minus-older effects. These are fitted-target diagnostics; neither their sign nor their change establishes a validation gain. Preserve actual module training flags and global RNG states; use no_grad and isolated generators. Include measured metrics, definitions, missingness, and limitations in the interpreter prompt.

Run all four categories for every compared arm on a single GPU. This requires twelve category fits if no equivalent baseline is reusable. Before launching each arm, require a declared compute ceiling that fits the externally tracked remaining 43,200 GPU-second budget, including diagnostics, failures, and debugging. Remaining budget is not provided here; do not assume the full budget remains or claim the experiment has completed. Keep checkpoint and validation-query schedules identical across arms. Report every observed category HR@10 and its equally weighted macro; choose the best complete arm using only the pinned host results. If paired host hits are available, summarize paired category differences and stratified user-bootstrap intervals, explicitly conditional on fixed models and candidates. Otherwise report aggregate comparisons without reconstructed labels. Four categories and one training seed support only limited exploratory conclusions.

Generate the required full-catalog unseen-item recommendations for five real training users/category. Use histories, titles, descriptions, and timestamps only. Treat ownership, compatibility, simulator traits, and preference judgments as unobserved unless explicitly supported by permitted evidence.

originality.positive: The explicitly routed, controlled comparison connects position-preserving behavioral probes to a narrowly specified component-level training intervention.
originality.negative: Embedding dropout, matched controls, and perturbation audits are established techniques; no new architectural mechanism or empirical advantage is established.

future_potential.positive: A completed experiment could establish a reusable foundation for testing whether positional regularization changes ranking behavior consistently across recommendation domains.
future_potential.negative: Generic regularization effects, fitted diagnostic targets, four heterogeneous categories, and one training seed limit mechanistic interpretation and generalization.

code_difficulty.positive: The training change is small and evaluation uses the existing SASRec scoring architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Correct routing, frozen cross-model probes, predictor reconstruction, and twelve potential category fits create integration and budget demands.

related_work.title: Towards Best Practices of Activation Patching in Language Models: Metrics and Methods
contributions: Demonstrates that corruption methods and measurement choices affect activation-patching conclusions.
Motivates explicit intervention definitions and controls for diagnostic interpretation.
limitations: Studies language models rather than the matched SASRec task.
Does not establish that positional dropout improves recommendation accuracy.

related_work.title: Learning Positional Attention for Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Investigates positional information in sequential recommendation and motivates separating positional relations from item semantics.
limitations: Its architectural findings do not establish positional overreliance in the supplied checkpoints.
Does not validate the proposed dropout probability or diagnostic selection rule.

related_work.title: On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Shows that sampled ranking metrics can disagree with full-catalog comparisons.
Supports distinguishing sampled training diagnostics, pinned benchmark selection, and full-catalog recommendation behavior.
limitations: Does not identify the cause of Electronics training-pair errors.
Does not justify changing the task's pinned validation evaluator.
